subject: Multiple Plots Against Columns in Dataframe with plyr

messages.subject: Multiple Plots Against Columns in Dataframe with plyr
parts:
Hello,

I'm certain that there is a way to do this, but I have not been able to
figure it out just yet. I have a dataframe for which I would like to
generate multiple bwplots and place them into a single pdf document like
the example on page 13 of the plyr vignette. The dataframe has column
'id' which I want plotted against each of columns 'C:Z'.

For example, bwplot(id ~ X, data = df) where X is one of 80 columns in
the dataframe, df. I thought there would be a way to get d_plyr to do
this but I'm not coming up with it. If anyone has any pointers I would
greatly appreciate it.

Thanks, Aric

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Plots Against Columns in Dataframe with plyr
parts:
Hi,

I'm not sure whether you want all plots on the same page or each in
its own page.
In either case I'd start by melting the data.frame into long format.

library(ggplot2)

d = data.frame(id = seq(1, 100), matrix(rnorm(100 * 5), ncol = 5))

m = melt(d, id="id")

plotone = function(.d) qplot(id, value, data=.d, geom="line")

pdf("one.pdf")
qplot(id, value, data=m, geom="line") + facet_wrap(~variable, ncol=1)
dev.off()


pdf("multiple.pdf")
d_ply(m, .(variable), plotone, .print=TRUE)
dev.off()

HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Plots Against Columns in Dataframe with plyr
parts:
I don't know if **ply can pass the name of the objects given to the
function; i doubt it. In your situation I'd do a for loop, maybe with
l*ply,

library(ggplot2)

basic <- ggplot() + geom_line(aes(id, value))

plotone <- function(.col) basic %+% subset(m, variable == .col) + ylab(.col)

pdf("multiple.pdf")
l_ply(unique(m$variable), plotone, .print=T)
dev.off()

Alternatively, you could loop over the original wide format data.frame,

plotone <- function(.col) ggplot(d) +
geom_line(aes_string(x="id", y=.col))

pdf("multiple.pdf")
l_ply(names(d)[-1], plotone, .print=T)
dev.off()

HTH,

baptiste
